prompt_md: Retrieval quality with an E5 model is oddly poor. You notice queries are embedded as plain text. Likely fix?

options.md: Add the `query: ` prefix to queries and `passage: ` to documents, then re-embed
options.why_md: Right. The prefixes are part of how the model was trained.
That hides the problem without fixing the embeddings.

hints: Which idea applies? Choose an embedding model by language and domain, max input, dimensions and cost.
solution_md: Right. The prefixes are part of how the model was trained.

prompt_md: When should you choose an embedding model with **fewer** dimensions?

options.md: When an eval on your data shows similar quality and memory or latency matters
options.why_md: Right. Measure, then take the cheaper option.

options.md: Never. More dimensions are always better
options.why_md: More dimensions cost memory and don't guarantee quality.
Language coverage is a separate question.

hints: Which idea applies? Choose an embedding model by language and domain, max input, dimensions and cost.
solution_md: Dimensions are a cost. Pay for them only when the eval says they buy quality.

prompt_md: You truncate a Matryoshka-trained 1,024-d vector to its first 256 numbers. What must you do before comparing with cosine-as-dot?

options.md: Re-normalize the truncated vector to length 1
options.why_md: Right. Truncation shortens the vector, so dot ≠ cosine until you re-normalize.
Its length is now below 1, so the dot product would be distorted.

options.md: Pad it back to 1,024 with zeros
options.why_md: Padding doesn't change the length problem, and it wastes memory.

hints: Which idea applies? Choose an embedding model by language and domain, max input, dimensions and cost.
OpenAI's docs say the same: if you shorten manually, normalize the result.
solution_md: OpenAI's docs say the same: if you shorten manually, normalize the result.
